subject: Provenance vs persisted: clarification on what Redwood keeps by default
messages:
From: BrightBank Security Team <security@brightbank.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-06-14T13:12:00Z
Subject: Clarify what is persisted vs provenance metadata

Hi Jasmine / Kimberly,

We’re finalizing BrightBank’s security review and need clarity on a couple of retention points before Legal signs off. Specifically:

1) "Provenance" vs persisted content — does Redwood store request headers/metadata (user id, model id, timestamps) separately from the user prompt and model response?
2) Streaming fragments and KV cache — are partial streamed tokens saved anywhere beyond the session?
3) Derived artifacts (summaries, tool outputs) — are those treated as persisted outputs or ephemeral derivatives?
4) Proof-of-deletion — if we ask for erasure, what evidence do you provide and how long after the request does deletion complete?

Can you send a concise mapping (what we keep by default, default TTL, exceptions for EU residency, and how enterprise retention commitments differ)? If you have a simple matrix or short SLA text we can drop into the questionnaire, that would be ideal.

We’d like to resolve this by EOD Thursday if possible.

Thanks,
David Wright
BrightBank – Platform Security
security@brightbank.com

Hi David — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise mapping you can paste into the questionnaire; attaching a compact retention matrix as well. Happy to join a short call to walk through.

High-level defaults (Hosted Redwood API):
- Provenance / telemetry metadata (persisted): model_id, region, request_timestamp, route_id, request_size, response_size, error flags. Default TTL: 365 days for audit telemetry; shorter retention can be configured for enterprise tenants.
- Request content (user prompt / inputs): Default TTL: 30 days. Purpose: debugging, quality monitoring, and customer support.
- Model responses (final outputs): Default TTL: 30 days. Purpose: customer-visible answers and debugging for production issues.
- Streamed fragments (partial tokens / intermediate buffers): Ephemeral by default; retained for a short buffering window only. Default TTL: 24 hours. They are not indexed and are pruned automatically; they are not considered part of the persistent artifact set.
- KV cache / runtime-only caches: In-memory by design; not persisted to long-term logs. Default runtime TTL: minutes to hours (configurable at the runtime level). Not included in the 30-day request/response logs.
- Derived artifacts (structured outputs, summaries, reranks): Treated as persisted artifacts by default because many customers surface these as results. Default TTL: 90 days. If a customer wants these treated as ephemeral, we can configure auto-flush/purge or exclude them from archiving.

Exceptions & residency:
- EU data residency: if a customer elects EU residency, all persisted records are stored only in EU regions and follow the same default TTLs unless you sign a retention SLA with custom TTLs.
- Compliance holds / legal holds: retention may be extended when a legal/compliance hold is in place; we provide notification and an explanation.

Proof of deletion & erasure flow:
1) Customer requests erasure via Console/Support or a signed request.
2) We mark records for targeted deletion and run a deterministic expunge job across replicas.
3) Standard request/response deletion completes within 72 hours for hosted accounts; full storage wiping (including backups) completes on the next backup cycle and we provide a deletion token and timestamp.
4) For EU residency or Dedicated/Private deployments, timelines can be contractually shortened and we can provide deletion certificates.

Attachments: retention-matrix.xlsx (compact mapping of item -> default TTL -> retention reason -> how to opt-out). Also attaching a redacted SOC2 reference (SOC2_redacted.pdf).

If that looks good I can loop in Legal/Procurement to propose BrightBank-specific retention commitments (e.g., 90-day default for persisted outputs and guaranteed purge within 48 hours for erasure requests). Suggest a 30-minute call Friday morning to finalize.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple of quick clarifications before we loop Legal:
- Confirm KV cache is never written to persisted logs/backups (Jasmine indicated runtime-only; want explicit confirmation).
- For streamed fragments: 24h buffer sounds reasonable; please confirm those are not searchable/indexed and are excluded from analytics exports.
- For deletion token: we need the deletion token + timestamp and a simple statement that backups will be wiped on next backup cycle (approx timeline). If you can share the SOC2 redacted file and the retention matrix (we received them in the attachments), we’ll schedule a legal review call.

If all of the above is explicit in the retention annex we should be ready to sign. Can you confirm KV cache and streamed fragment indexing behavior?

David
